title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows an impersonation attack using AI-generated videos to assume the identity of a real person and commit fraud. The failure occurred in the social media platform layer, where fake accounts and synthetic media impersonating a named attorney were posted and remained discoverable for months before removal. It would have taken either automated detection of identity impersonation at upload time, human review of accounts claiming to be licensed professionals, or verification mechanisms for users offering paid legal services.

The scam targeted a vulnerable population by exploiting two gaps: the difficulty of verifying professional credentials online, and the trust immigrants may place in someone appearing to offer legal assistance. The victims were directed off-platform to messaging apps and payment services where the fraud was completed, making it harder for social media platforms to detect and intervene.

It is not established whether the social media platforms had policies against this activity or whether the attorney had reported the accounts before the anti-piracy company's intervention.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
# Summary

Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating Leal to defraud people seeking immigration services. In these videos, the fake Leal offers services such as US residency assistance for $2,200 and claims to help immigrants avoid deportation. The scam typically directs victims through social media to contact a WhatsApp number, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payments through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office with questions about services he never offered. Although suspicious activity began last October, the problem escalated dramatically over the past three months. Leal hired an anti-piracy company that removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. Leal is warning immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of requests for immediate payment through digital apps.
